method.code: diagnostic copy of the deployed r141 package, only pipeline_worker.py patched with prof_start/prof_stop/inventory RPCs
method.window: decode: 32 profiled steps, 31 token periods accounted between consecutive step ends; prefill: one chunk interval
method.closure: width = device_busy + intra_stage_gap + outer_host_gap (per token period)

candidates.what: Fuse the DeltaNet q/k l2norm chain (mul, sum, add, rsqrt, mul: 5 kernels x 72 per token, ~1.25 ms measured) into one kernel.
candidates.evidence: sum_order_probe.py: a hand-written fp32 sum over the last dim of [64,16,128] reproduces torch ReduceSum bitwise on at most 72.9% of rows (best order: block8+tree; sequential 25.8%). No association order tested matches, so the fusion cannot preserve the FP32 reduction order.

candidates.what: Double-buffer the expert gather (2 x 40 KiB UB staging buffers) so the MTE2 load of the next tile overlaps the MTE3 store of the current one; output bytes unchanged.
candidates.evidence: component A/B (probe_gather.py): gu 13.75 -> 12.46 us (1.10x), dn 7.09 -> 7.10 us (1.00x). Real L00 decode graph (layer_probe.py, 8 replays x 5): deployed 1.91346 ms vs double-buffered 1.91374 ms, i.e. no gain; output, FP32 state and BF16 conv history bitwise identical.

side_finding.what: The deployed libfnx_expert_gather.so (sha256 b7c4eaef...) is not reproducible from kernels/expert_gather/gather.cpp: a rebuild (5e9457b1...) and the double-buffered variant (fc68d351...) both match a torch reference on a standalone intake probe (3/3 deterministic) for the K=2560/G=40/N=1280 shape, while the deployed binary is non-deterministic and does not match the reference there.
side_finding.model_impact: In the real L00 decode graph all three binaries give bitwise-identical outputs, so production numerics are unaffected in the verified path; the discrepancy is not deployed and is left for follow-up.

prefill.status: see prefill section of the report; 512-token early chunk shows MoE grouped GMM at 58% of device time

notes: TTFT and TPOT were not re-measured through HTTP in this round; production numbers are the r141 acceptance (8k TPOT 34.75 ms, 256k TPOT 35.99 ms).
The profiled decode windows run 1.2-3.6% slower than the unprofiled baseline in the same process (profiler overhead), so the ledger is used for attribution, not as a target number.
Two cards do not overlap in decode: stage0 and stage1 execute serially, so per-token device time is the sum of both stages.
